question.worked_solution:
We need to isolate the variable $x.$ To do this, we treat $y$ as though it were a constant and apply the addition and multiplication principles as usual.

First, we add $y$ to both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-y & =y-x \\ 2x-y+y & =y-x+y \\ 2x & =-x+2y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we add $x$ to both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =-x+2y \\ 2x+x & =-x+2y+x \\ 3x & =2y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide both sides of the equation by $3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3x & =2y \\ \frac{3x}{3} & =\frac{2y}{3} \\ \frac{\cancel{3}x}{\cancel{3}} & =\frac{2y}{3} \\ x & =\frac{2y}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
